chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:

I entered upon Abu Ja'far ibn al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I want to press my belly against your belly.' He said, 'Here, O Abu Ismail,' and he uncovered his belly. I uncovered my belly and pressed it against his. Then he seated me and called for a platter containing raisins, so I ate. Then he began speaking and complained to me about his stomach. I was thirsty, so I fetched water. He said, 'O Maid! Give him a drink from my nabidh.'

She brought me nabidh made from partially-ripened dates in a yellow cup. I drank it and found it sweeter than honey. I said to him, 'This is what spoils your stomach.' He said to me, 'These are dates from the charity of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). They are taken in the morning, water is poured over them, the maid soaks them, and I drink them after the meal and throughout the rest of my day. When it is night, the maid takes it and gives it to the people of the house to drink.'

I said to him, 'The people of Kufa are not satisfied with this.' He said, 'And what is their nabidh?' I said, 'They take the dates, clean them, and pour Al-Qa'wa over them.' He said, 'And what is Al-Qa'wa?' I said, 'Al-Daazy.' He said, 'And what is Al-Daazy?' I said, 'A grain brought from Basra, which is poured into this nabidh until it boils and intoxicates, then it is drunk.' He said, 'That is prohibited.'

key_terms.الدَّاذِيُّ: Al-Daazy: A grain brought from Basra used to induce intoxication in the drink.
key_terms.الْقَعْوَةُ: Al-Qa'wa: A specific ingredient or method used in preparing the Kufan nabidh.
key_terms.صَدَقَة: Sadaqah: Charity or alms, here referring to dates given to the Prophet.
key_terms.نَبِيذ: Nabidh: A drink made by soaking dates or raisins in water.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the permissible nabidh of the Ahl al-Bayt and the intoxicating nabidh of the Kufans?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s practical distinction between permissible *nabidh* and intoxicants by contrasting his method of consuming fresh, non-intoxicating date water with the Kufan practice of adding *Al-Daazy* (a grain from Basra) to induce intoxication. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the substance and preparation method as determinants for permissibility, linking the physical act of drinking to the spiritual state of sobriety. The narrative also illustrates the Imam’s generosity and the communal sharing of blessed sustenance, reinforcing the social dimension of dietary laws in early Islamic tradition.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Bin Abu al Balaad who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ja’farasws Bin Al-Rezaasws, so I said to himasws, ‘I want that my belly touches yourasws belly’. So heasws said: ‘Over here, O Abu Ismail’, and heasws uncovered hisasws belly and I uncovered from my belly, and my belly and hisasws belly touched. Then heasws made me sit and called for a platter in which were raisings. So I ate, then heasws started discussing, so heasws complained to me about hisasws stomach, and I was thirsty, so I asked for water. So heasws said : ‘O Maid! Give him a drink from myasws Nabeez’.

So she came to me with Nabeez of partially-ripened dates in a yellow cup. So I drank it and found it to be sweeter than the honey. So I said to himasws, ‘This is which spoils yourasws stomach’. So heasws said to me: ‘These dates are from the donation of the Prophetsaww. It is taken in the morning, and water is poured over it, and the maid soaks it, and I drink it upon the effects of the meal, and rest of myasws day. So when it was the night, the maid takes it, so she gives it to the people of the house to drink’.

So I said to himasws, ‘The people of Al-Kufa are not happy with this’. So heasws said: ‘And what is their Nabeez?’ I said, ‘They take the dates, and they clean them and cast Al-Qa’wa over it’. Heasws said: ‘And what is Al-Qa’wa?’ I said, ‘Al-Daazy’. Heasws said: ‘And what is Al-Baazy?’ I said, ‘A grain which they come with from Al-Basra, so it is cast into this Al-Nabeez until it boil and it intoxicates. Then they drink it’. So heasws said: ‘That is Prohibited’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad who has said the following:

“I once visited abu Ja‘far, ibn al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said to him, ‘I want to touch your belly with my belly.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Here O abu Tsma‘il,’ He uncovered his belly and I uncovered my belly and touched his belly with my belly. He then made me sit and called for a plate of raisins. I ate and he began to speak and complained about his stomach. I felt thisty and asked for water. He (the Imam) said, ‘O Jariyah, give him from my al-Nabidh.

She brought for me al-Nabidh of Maris (soaked) in a cup of brass. I drank and found it sweeter than honey. I then said to him, ‘This has made your stomach upset.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is dates from the charity of the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. It is taken in the morning and water is poured on it. The girl soaks it and I drink it after food and during the day. In the evening the girl takes it and the people of the house drink.’

I then said, ‘People of al-Kufah do not agree with it.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is their al-Nabidh?’ I said, ‘It is taken from dates of finiqiy and al-Qa‘wah is placed in it.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is al-Qa‘wah?’ I said, ‘It is al- Dadhiy.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is al-Dadhiy?’ I said, ‘It is grain which is brought from al- Basrah. It is thrown in al-Nabidh until it boils and becomes intoxicating liquor; then it is used as a drink.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘That is unlawful.’”
